_note: v2 hook overrides for la Grande Serre (B64_serre). Source hooks are kept wherever the painting shows them; these replace only hooks whose painted scene differs from the source text, or that repeat a motif (caterpillar/butterfly, snail, gardener) used by another word in this building, so each card describes exactly what is in the picture.

fr_changement_noun.hook: Like English 'change', said shahn-zhuh-MAHN: a chameleon on a greenhouse flowerpot goes through a big CHANGE, turning from leaf-green to bright pink.
fr_changement_noun.why: The butterfly motif is kept for la transition in the stump; a colour-changing chameleon is painted here so the two words do not share a picture.

fr_formation_noun.hook: Like English 'formation', said for-mah-SYOHN: three seedlings stand in perfect FORMATION on the bench while a toy TRAINING sergeant in a tall drill hat waters them.
fr_formation_noun.why: Painted as three seedlings in a row with a toy sergeant (no marching band).

fr_transformation_noun.hook: Like English 'transformation', said trahns-for-mah-SYOHN: a pumpkin on the greenhouse floor undergoes a magic TRANSFORMATION into a golden carriage.
fr_transformation_noun.why: Replaces a second caterpillar-to-butterfly scene (used for la transition) with the pumpkin carriage that is painted.

fr_reforme_noun.hook: Like English 'reform', said ray-FORM: the gardener's shears have trimmed a round bush into the FORM of a manta RAY ("RAY-FORM"), its wide fins spread as if gliding across the floor.
fr_reforme_noun.why: Owner review: the bush is now clipped into the form of a manta ray (was a swan).

fr_pousse_noun.hook: A green SHOOT pushes ("pouss") up out of its pot so hard that it lifts a big round pebble on its head.
fr_pousse_noun.why: The painted shoot lifts a pebble; the pebble makes the push visible.

fr_transparence_noun.hook: Like English 'transparency', said trahns-pah-RAHNS: the greenhouse glass has such TRANSPARENCY that a sparrow flutters at it, puzzled, unable to see it is there.
fr_transparence_noun.why: No PA or stickers are painted; just the puzzled sparrow at the clear glass.

fr_transition_noun.hook: Like English 'transition', said trahn-zee-SYOHN: on the old stump a butterfly makes the TRANSITION out of its chrysalis, stretching new orange wings with a sigh.
fr_transition_noun.why: Painted as the butterfly emerging from the chrysalis (the caterpillar stage is not shown).

fr_hausse_noun.hook: Prices RISE: a toy horse ("oss") climbs a staircase of flowerpots, each one higher than the last.
fr_hausse_noun.why: The steps are painted as rising flowerpots; the painting has no numbers.

fr_amelioration_noun.hook: A scruffy garden patch makes a big IMPROVEMENT ("ah-may-lyoh-rah-SYOHN"): weeds on one half, neat bright flowers on the other, the rake that did the work lying beside it.
fr_amelioration_noun.why: The gardener is left out (a gardener already appears upstairs); the before/after patch and rake show the improvement.

fr_alternative_noun.hook: Like English 'alternative', said ahl-tehr-nah-TEEV: a girl offers the slugs an ALTERNATIVE to her plants: a lettuce of their own in a separate pot.
fr_alternative_noun.why: The gardener is painted as a girl holding out the lettuce pot to two slugs.

fr_revision_noun.hook: Like English 'revision', said ray-vee-ZYOHN: the garden plan pinned on the cork board is covered in REVISIONS, arrows and crossings-out, after the moles below it moved things.
fr_revision_noun.why: The plan is pinned on a board with the two moles on the shelf beneath, rather than held by a gardener.

fr_emprise_noun.hook: A frosty wind giant blows an icy breeze ("ahn-PREEZ") from the corner and holds the attic in his GRIP: the roses on the shelf freeze stiff with icicles.
fr_emprise_noun.why: The painting shows the giant gripping the greenhouse attic and its frozen roses, not a whole village.

fr_avancee_noun.hook: Like English 'advance', said ah-vahn-SAY: a tortoise with a backpack makes a great ADVANCE across the attic floor: a few whole planks in a single morning.
fr_avancee_noun.why: A tortoise replaces the snail, which is already le progrès on the glass downstairs.

fr_remplacement_noun.hook: Like English 'replacement', said rahn-plah-suh-MAHN: the wheelbarrow has lost its wheel, and a REPLACEMENT wheel rolls up the RAMP into PLACE.
fr_remplacement_noun.why: No mechanic is painted; the wheel rolls up the plank to the wheel-less barrow on its own.

fr_avancement_noun.hook: Like English 'advancement', said ah-vahn-suh-MAHN: a beanstalk tied with prize ribbons shows its ADVANCEMENT: it has grown right up through the greenhouse roof.
fr_avancement_noun.why: The ribbons mark its progress instead of a chart.

fr_epanouissement_noun.hook: In a frying PAN on the stove we see ("ay-pah-nwee-suh") a big red rose BLOOMING, unfolding petal by petal.
fr_epanouissement_noun.why: Owner review: the odd line about a cook is removed.

fr_confection_noun.hook: Not "confection": confection (kohn-fehk-SYOHN) is MAKING; a hedgehog crafts a wreath by hand.
fr_confection_noun.why: A hedgehog makes the wreath, since the girl gardener is already l'alternative.

fr_alternance_noun.hook: Like English 'alternance', said ahl-tehr-NAHNS: an ALTERNATION of sun and rain: a frog holds an umbrella in one hand and sunglasses in the other, ready to switch.
fr_alternance_noun.why: Shows both items at once so the switching is visible in one picture.

fr_substitution_noun.hook: Like English 'substitution', said sewp-stee-tew-SYOHN: a toy SUBmarine in a tray of water gets a SUBSTITUTE periscope: the old one lies on the floor and a shiny new one stands in its place.
fr_substitution_noun.why: Owner review: the substitution is now done on a submarine (was a snowman's nose).

fr_alteration_noun.hook: Like English 'alteration', said ahl-tay-rah-SYOHN: a little mouse tailor makes an ALTERATION to a scarecrow's jacket, pinning on a bright new patch.
fr_alteration_noun.why: The painted alteration is a new patch on the jacket, not a new hat and nose.

fr_accroissement_noun.hook: A big crow perches on top of a tall notched height post: the crow GROWS and GROWS until the crow's a man ("a-krwas-MAN") in height.
fr_accroissement_noun.why: The growth chart is painted as a notched height post.

fr_grandissant_adj.hook: A grand sun ("grahn-dee-SAHN") glows in the round attic window and keeps GROWING bigger and bigger.
fr_grandissant_adj.why: The sun is painted in the round window rather than over a horizon.
